paper.title: A Diffusion-Based Pre-training Framework for Crystal Property Prediction
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes CrysDiff, a diffusion-based pretrain-finetune framework to address the scarcity of labeled crystal property data. In pre-training, it reconstructs crystal structures (lattice and fractional coordinates) from atom compositions using a joint denoising diffusion model with EGNN to preserve crystal symmetries. In fine-tuning, it models the conditional distribution of target properties given crystal structures by diffusing on the property value while keeping the structure fixed.

tasks.objective: Predict a target property value y ∈ R based on its 3D crystal structure (A, F, L)
constraints: limited labeled data due to expensive physical simulations or lab experiments
must satisfy O(3) invariance and periodic translation invariance
input_requirements: 3D crystal structure represented as atom features A, fractional coordinates F, and lattice matrix L

evidence.text: The crystal property prediction aims to predict a target property value y ∈R based on its structure (A, F, L).

stages.stage_goal: Acquire large-scale unlabeled 3D crystal structure data for pre-training
stage_output: 800K untagged crystal graph data from Materials Project (MP) and OQMD

evidence.text: We collect 800K untagged crystal graph data from two popular materials databases, Materials Project (MP) (Jain et al. 2013) and OQMD (Saal et al. 2013), to pre-train the CrysDiff model.

stages.stage_goal: Acquire labeled crystal structure–property pairs for fine-tuning and evaluation
stage_output: OQMD-EXP dataset (1,500 experimental formation energy values)

evidence.text: Further, to evaluate the fine-tuning performance of CrysDiff compared with other crystal property predictors, we select the 2021.8.18 version of JARVIS-DFT (Choudhary et al. 2020), another popular materials database, for the downstream property prediction task. JARVIS-DFT consists of 55,722 materials with 19 properties, like formation energy, bandgap, total energy, bulk modulus, etc., which depend significantly on crystal structures and atom features.
Therefore, to investigate how our model helps to mitigate the DFT error, we also take a small dataset OQMD-EXP (Kirklin et al. 2015), containing 1,500 available experimental data of formation energy.

stages.stage_goal: Learn the latent marginal distribution p(F, L | A) of crystal structures using self-supervised diffusion
stage_input: unlabeled crystal structure data (A, F0, L0)

evidence.text: In the pre-training phase, CrysDiff learns the latent marginal distribution of crystal structures via the reconstruction task.
In the pre-training phase, we perform the task of crystal structure reconstruction to model the distribution p(F, L | A) based on the diffusion model from a large amount of unlabeled data.

stages.stage_goal: Adapt the pre-trained model to learn the conditional distribution p(y | A′, F′, L′) using sparse labeled data
stage_input: labeled crystal structure–property pairs (A′, F′, L′, y)

evidence.text: Subsequently, CrysDiff can be fine-tuned under the guidance of the new sparse labeled data, fitting the conditional distribution of the target property given the crystal structures.

To fully leverage the knowledge about the crystal structure during the pre-training phase, we stick to the backbone diffusion model when fine-tuning. However, the downstream task becomes a deterministic task. Hence, we aim to model p(y | A′, F′, L′) with the newly observed labeled data, following the previous work (Han, Zheng, and Zhou 2022).

stages.stage_goal: Evaluate fine-tuned model performance on multiple crystal properties using MAE
stage_input: test set from JARVIS-DFT and OQMD-EXP
stage_output: MAE scores for nine properties on JARVIS-DFT
MAE scores for formation energy on OQMD-EXP

evidence.text: We report mean absolute error (MAE) of the predicted and actual value of a particular property to compare the performance of different participating methods.
